 MADISON, Wis. — The Wisconsin Department of Motor Vehicles' customer service centers will extend their hours Monday and Tuesday to help voters obtain photo identification for the state's midterm election.
 Locations will remain open until 6 p.m. Tuesday.
 What you need to know before Tuesday's election 
 The extended hours are intended for voters who do not already have a Wisconsin driver's license, state ID card or another acceptable form of identification.
 To obtain a Wisconsin ID card, residents must provide a birth certificate, proof of identity and proof of Wisconsin residency. The DMV provides ID cards for voting to U.S. citizens at no charge.
 Wisconsin does not require a separate “voter ID,” and a federally compliant REAL ID is not required to vote.
 For voters who cannot complete the process before polls open, the DMV will send a photo ID document by overnight mail that can be used to vote. Voters may also cast a provisional ballot while waiting for their ID to arrive.
 Voter Resources 
 Questions about obtaining an ID for voting can be directed to the DMV's toll-free hotline (844) 588-1069, and election information is available on the Wisconsin Elections Commission website .
